title: Typed schema bridge and async-parse cookbook for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Users struggle to author robust streaming consumers and typed response models when upgrading between dataclass-first and pydantic-first patterns. The current SDK has multiple ad-hoc helpers that are hard to compose with async iterators, retrying callers, and gradual schema migration. Goal: Provide a single 'typed schema bridge' library and cookbook that demonstrates best-practice patterns for (1) defining model contracts with Protocols and lightweight adapters, (2) incremental migration tooling to generate shim adapters between pydantic models and dataclasses, and (3) ergonomic async-parsing helpers that support backpressure, checkpointing, and idempotent retries in streaming contexts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A stable typed-schema-bridge module checked into python-sdk with public functions: adapt_pydantic_to_dataclass, adapt_dataclass_to_pydantic, stream_async_parse, and retry_safe_reconstructor. 2) Three runnable examples in examples/typed_bridge demonstrating: (a) simple generation -> typed dataclass output, (b) long-running streaming chat with checkpoint resume and exactly-once reassembly, (c) migration scenario where an existing pydantic model is replaced by a dataclass and adapters keep compatibility. 3) Unit tests covering adapter edge cases and property-preserving roundtrip. 4) Doc page and notebook in docs/ explaining trade-offs and quickstart.
design_notes: High-level design: - Use typing.Protocol for the canonical interface consumers rely on (StreamSerializable[T]). This avoids exporting heavy runtime types. - Implement thin adapter functions that perform zero-copy where possible (mapping simple fields) and shallow-copy with validation only when crossing runtime boundaries (pydantic -> dataclass or vice versa). - Provide stream_async_parse that accepts an AsyncIterator[bytes|str|EventChunk], a parser callable, and yields hydrated typed objects. The helper should expose checkpoint tokens and a small resume protocol so callers can resume parsing mid-stream after a retry. - For retries: implement retry_safe_reconstructor that replays idempotent parts of the stream and skips already-processed checkpoints. Integrate with existing retry/backoff utilities in the SDK. - Prefer deterministic ordering: adapters must preserve field order for stable diffs in evals and regression tests.
tradeoffs: 1) Runtime cost vs ergonomics: validating pydantic during every adapter call is expensive; we default to lazy validation with an optional strict flag. 2) Complexity: adding a resume protocol increases surface area; mitigated by keeping default behavior simple and making resume explicit. 3) API choices: exposing Protocols keeps typing ergonomics good for users but requires careful docs to avoid misuse.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Week 1): prototype typed_protocols and basic adapter functions, land feature-flagged module. Phase 2 (Week 2): implement stream_async_parse with checkpoint/resume; add unit tests for edge cases. Phase 3 (Week 3): write examples, docs, and SDK integration (expose in public package). Phase 4 (Week 4): dogfood on internal infra jobs and iterate on perf hotspots (profile adapter + parse).
testing_plan: - Unit tests for adapter roundtrips, nullable fields, union fields, and JSON alias handling. - Integration tests using a fake streaming generator to simulate partial chunks, reorder, and duplicate segments to validate idempotency. - Performance microbenchmarks to compare lazy validation vs strict validation. - E2E example runs using the examples/typed_bridge notebooks. - Add CI gates: 95% coverage for the new module and regression test against a golden-output fixture.
rollout_plan: Stage behind feature flag: python-sdk.experimental.0.1.0. Start internal alpha with platform-integrations and set a one-week dogfood period. Monitor errors and latency on demo routes. After signoff, flip flag for GA in python-sdk-2026.03. Deprecation: publish migration guide for existing helper functions with 2 release window before removal.
metrics_and_observability: Instrument adapter invocation counts, average per-item parse latency, validation rate (strict vs lazy), and checkpoint resume frequency. Add logs for resume failures and attach trace IDs so Console can surface correlated traces. Set an alert if resume failure rate > 0.5% on alpha routes.
rollback_plan: If production issues occur (data loss or incorrect schema hydration), immediately revert to previous adapter entrypoints by toggling feature flag off. Maintain a runbook to extract in-flight checkpoints and reprocess streams with the legacy parser.
